title: Why noise cancelling leaves the conversation
script:
Noise cancelling on. So why can you still hear that conversation?

Your headphones make another sound.
Microphones listen to the noise. A processor drives the speaker to produce counter-sound.
At your ear, those pressure changes partly cancel.

The tricky part is making them line up.
Low-pitched rumble is a good target. Voices keep changing, across a wider range of frequencies. Some speech can still get through.

And the electronics have help. The ear cups or ear tips form a physical barrier too. That seal matters.

So hearing the person beside you doesn't automatically mean your headphones are broken.
They can turn down the commute without muting it.

Follow TechWhoKnows for the tech hiding in plain sight.
